transcript.text: bosch washer FD 9409 not draining. ive cleaned the filter already. what part do i need?

FD 9409 is the production date, not the model number. Bosch FD codes work like this: the first two digits minus 80 give the year, and the last two give the month. So FD 9409 = built September 2014. To order the correct part, you need the E-Nr (e.g. WAT28400GB/05 or WAQ24468GB/01), including the number after the slash. It's on the rating plate, usually on the inside rim of the door opening, the inside of the door, or behind the filter flap.

## Most likely part: the drain pump

If the filter is clean and it still won't drain, the drain pump is the usual culprit. Before buying one, do a few quick checks.

1. Listen when it tries to drain (run a "Drain" or "Spin" program):
• Humming but no water moving → the impeller is jammed or broken, or the pump is failing.
• Completely silent → the pump is dead, or there's a wiring or control issue.
• Pump runs normally → the blockage is likely elsewhere (see below).

2. Check the impeller. With the filter removed, shine a torch into the filter opening. You should see the pump impeller. Turn it with a finger:
• It should turn in jerky steps (that's normal for the magnetic rotor).
• If it's jammed, look for coins, hair grips, or bra wires.
• If it spins completely freely with no resistance, or is snapped, the pump needs replacing.

3. Rule out other blockages:
• Drain hose: look for kinks behind the machine, or blow through it.
• Sink trap or spigot: if the washer drains into a sink waste, the connection often clogs or still has a blanking cap fitted after new plumbing work.
• Standpipe: check for blockage.
• Sump hose (between the drum and the pump): socks can lodge here. Reach it by tilting the machine back or removing the front kickplate.

4. Note any error code. E18 / F18 (or "Check drain" or the tap symbol) indicates a drain fault on most Bosch models of that age.

## Ordering the pump

Search the E-Nr + "drain pump" on Bosch's official parts site (bosch-home.com → Spare Parts) or a parts retailer. Most 2014-era Bosch pumps cost about £20–£40 and are easy to fit: usually 2–3 screws or clips, two hose clips, and an electrical plug.

Safety: unplug the machine and drain any remaining water through the filter/emergency hose (have towels and a shallow tray ready) before working on it.

If you send me the E-Nr, I can help you work out exactly what to look for.
E-Nr label is rubbed off, can't read it. Pump hums but nothing moves, and it shows E18. Impeller turns but feels stiff and gritty. So is it the pump?

## Yes, it's almost certainly the pump

Humming with no water moving, an E18 code, and a stiff, gritty impeller point to a worn or failing drain pump. A healthy impeller turns in smooth, jerky "clicks" from the magnet. Grittiness usually means worn bearings or debris inside the motor, which leaves it too weak to spin under load. That causes the hum.

One quick thing to try first: with the filter out, flush the filter opening with a jug of warm water while turning the impeller by hand. If loose grit or sand comes out and it suddenly turns smoothly, try a Drain cycle again. If it's still gritty or still just hums, replace the pump.

## Identifying the part without the E-Nr

1. Read the number off the pump itself (most reliable).
Bosch pumps (usually made by Askoll or Hanning) have a sticker or moulded label with a part number. Once you remove the pump, photograph that label and search the number, or take the pump to a parts shop to match it.

2. Look for the E-Nr elsewhere:
• The user manual or installation guide
• The original receipt, delivery note, or online order history
• Your Bosch account, if you registered the appliance
• Other spots on the machine (back panel, inside the filter flap, door edge)

3. Contact Bosch customer service.
Give them the FD 9409 and a description of the machine. They can sometimes help narrow it down, though they'll usually ask for the E-Nr.

## Getting the pump out

1. Unplug the machine and turn off the water.
2. Drain the water first using the small emergency drain hose next to the filter. Use a shallow tray and towels, because there will be a lot of water.
3. Remove the kickplate (the plinth panel at the bottom front). On many 2014 Bosch models the pump is reachable from the front. On others, tilt the machine back carefully, or lay it on its side, and reach it from underneath.
4. The pump motor is often held on with a screw or two plus a twist-lock to the filter housing. Disconnect the wiring plug (photograph it first).

Tip: On many Bosch machines the motor twists off the filter/pump housing. You may only need the motor unit, not the whole housing assembly, which is cheaper. Compare your old part with the listing photos before ordering.

A replacement typically costs £20–£60 depending on genuine vs. compatible parts. It's a manageable DIY job if you're comfortable tilting the machine.
